{"schemaVersion":"turn-plan/v3","question":"Evaluate the definite integral of x sin x with respect to x from 0 to pi.","givens":[{"id":"f","symbol":"f(x)","value":0,"unit":"","sourceText":"integrand x sin x","provenance":"given"},{"id":"a","symbol":"a","value":0,"sourceText":"lower limit 0","provenance":"given"},{"id":"b","symbol":"b","value":3.141592653589793,"sourceText":"upper limit pi","provenance":"given"}],"unknowns":[{"id":"I","symbol":"I"}],"derived":[{"id":"I","symbol":"I","value":3.141592653589793,"sourceText":"∫0^π x sin x dx = [-x cos x + sin x]_0^π = π","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["f","a","b"]}],"qualitativeClaims":[{"id":"c1","claim":"Integration by parts with u=x, dv=sin x dx gives ∫ x sin x dx = -x cos x + sin x; evaluating from 0 to π yields π.","expected":"I = π ≈ 3.14159","relatedQuantityIds":["I"]}],"lawIds":["integration by parts","fundamental theorem of calculus"],"assumptions":["pi denotes the constant π"],"visualRequirement":"none"}

{"schemaVersion":"turn-plan/v3","question":"Find the y-intercept of the tangent to the curve y = x^3 - 2x at the point where x = 2.","givens":[{"id":"g1","symbol":"x","value":2,"sourceText":"x = 2","provenance":"given"}],"unknowns":[{"id":"u1","symbol":"b","unit":null}],"derived":[{"id":"d1","symbol":"y","value":4,"sourceText":"y = 2^3 - 2(2) = 8 - 4 = 4","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["g1"]},{"id":"d2","symbol":"m","value":10,"sourceText":"dy/dx = 3x^2 - 2; at x=2: 3(4) - 2 = 10","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["g1"]},{"id":"d3","symbol":"b","value":-16,"sourceText":"y = mx + b => 4 = 10(2) + b => b = 4 - 20 = -16","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["d1","d2"]}],"qualitativeClaims":[{"id":"c1","claim":"The tangent line at x=2 has slope 10 and passes through (2,4), crossing the y-axis at -16.","expected":"Tangent line: y = 10x - 16, y-intercept = -16","relatedQuantityIds":["d1","d2","d3"]}],"lawIds":["power-rule-differentiation","point-slope-form","tangent-line-equation"],"assumptions":["The curve is y = x^3 - 2x, differentiable everywhere."],"visualRequirement":"optional"}

{"schemaVersion":"turn-plan/v3","question":"Find the area enclosed between the curves y = x^2 and y = 2x.","givens":[{"id":"c1","symbol":"y","value":"x^2","sourceText":"y = x^2","provenance":"given"},{"id":"c2","symbol":"y","value":"2x","sourceText":"y = 2x","provenance":"given"}],"unknowns":[{"id":"A","symbol":"A","unit":"square units"}],"derived":[{"id":"x1","symbol":"x_1","value":0,"sourceText":"x^2 = 2x => x(x-2)=0 => x=0","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["c1","c2"]},{"id":"x2","symbol":"x_2","value":2,"sourceText":"x^2 = 2x => x(x-2)=0 => x=2","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["c1","c2"]},{"id":"A","symbol":"A","value":1.3333333333333333,"unit":"square units","sign":"positive","sourceText":"A = ∫_0^2 (2x - x^2) dx = [x^2 - x^3/3]_0^2 = 4 - 8/3 = 4/3","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["c1","c2","x1","x2"]}],"qualitativeClaims":[{"id":"cl1","claim":"The curves intersect where x^2 = 2x, giving x = 0 and x = 2 (points (0,0) and (2,4)).","expected":"intersection x-values 0 and 2","relatedQuantityIds":["x1","x2"]},{"id":"cl2","claim":"On the interval (0,2), the line y = 2x lies above the parabola y = x^2, so the integrand is 2x - x^2.","expected":"upper curve minus lower curve = 2x - x^2","relatedQuantityIds":["c1","c2"]},{"id":"cl3","claim":"The enclosed area equals the definite integral of (2x - x^2) from 0 to 2, which evaluates to 4/3 square units.","expected":"A = 4/3 ≈ 1.333","relatedQuantityIds":["A"]}],"lawIds":["definite-integral-area-between-curves","power-rule-integration","fundamental-theorem-of-calculus"],"assumptions":["Curves are graphed in the standard Cartesian plane with x horizontal and y vertical.","Area is measured in square units of the coordinate system."],"visualRequirement":"required"}

{"schemaVersion":"turn-plan/v3","question":"Evaluate the definite integral of x sin x with respect to x from 0 to pi.","givens":[{"id":"g1","symbol":"f(x)","value":"x sin x","sourceText":"integrand x sin x","provenance":"given"},{"id":"g2","symbol":"a","value":0,"sourceText":"lower limit 0","provenance":"given"},{"id":"g3","symbol":"b","value":3.141592653589793,"sourceText":"upper limit pi","provenance":"given"}],"unknowns":[{"id":"u1","symbol":"I","unit":null}],"derived":[{"id":"d1","symbol":"I","value":3.141592653589793,"sourceText":"∫_0^π x sin x dx = [-x cos x + sin x]_0^π = π","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["g1","g2","g3"]}],"qualitativeClaims":[{"id":"c1","claim":"Integration by parts with u=x, dv=sin x dx gives ∫ x sin x dx = -x cos x + sin x.","expected":"-x cos x + sin x","relatedQuantityIds":["u1"]},{"id":"c2","claim":"Evaluating the antiderivative at the bounds: at π, -π cos π + sin π = π; at 0, value is 0.","expected":"π - 0 = π","relatedQuantityIds":["d1","g2","g3"]}],"lawIds":["integration by parts","fundamental theorem of calculus"],"assumptions":["pi denotes the constant π","radian measure for the sine function"],"visualRequirement":"none"}

{"schemaVersion":"turn-plan/v3","question":"Find the acute angle in degrees between the lines y = 2x + 3 and y = -x + 1.","givens":[{"id":"m1","symbol":"m1","value":2,"sourceText":"y = 2x + 3","provenance":"given"},{"id":"m2","symbol":"m2","value":-1,"sourceText":"y = -x + 1","provenance":"given"}],"unknowns":[{"id":"theta","symbol":"θ","unit":"deg"}],"derived":[{"id":"theta","symbol":"θ","value":71.565,"unit":"deg","sourceText":"tanθ=|(2-(-1))/(1+2(-1))|=|3/-1|=3; θ=arctan(3)≈71.565°","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["m1","m2"]}],"qualitativeClaims":[{"id":"c1","claim":"Acute angle between lines of slopes m1,m2 satisfies tanθ=|(m1-m2)/(1+m1*m2)|","expected":"tanθ=|(m1-m2)/(1+m1*m2)|","relatedQuantityIds":["m1","m2","theta"]},{"id":"c2","claim":"Slopes 2 and -1 give tanθ=3, so θ=arctan(3)≈71.565°, which is acute","expected":"θ≈71.565°","relatedQuantityIds":["theta"]}],"lawIds":["angle_between_lines_slope_formula","arctan"],"assumptions":["Lines are in a standard Euclidean plane","Acute angle means the smaller angle at intersection, in (0°,90°]"],"visualRequirement":"optional"}

{"schemaVersion":"turn-plan/v3","question":"Find the y-intercept of the tangent to the curve y = x^3 - 2x at the point where x = 2.","givens":[{"id":"g1","symbol":"x","value":2,"sourceText":"x = 2","provenance":"given"}],"unknowns":[{"id":"u1","symbol":"b","unit":null}],"derived":[{"id":"d1","symbol":"y","value":4,"sourceText":"y = 2^3 - 2(2) = 8 - 4 = 4","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["g1"]},{"id":"d2","symbol":"m","value":10,"sourceText":"dy/dx = 3x^2 - 2; at x=2: 3(4) - 2 = 10","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["g1"]},{"id":"d3","symbol":"b","value":-16,"sourceText":"y = mx + b => 4 = 10(2) + b => b = 4 - 20 = -16","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["d1","d2"]}],"qualitativeClaims":[{"id":"c1","claim":"The tangent line at x=2 has slope 10 and passes through (2,4), crossing the y-axis at -16.","expected":"b = y - mx = 4 - 10(2) = -16","relatedQuantityIds":["d1","d2","d3"]}],"lawIds":["power-rule-differentiation","point-slope-tangent-line","y-intercept-definition"],"assumptions":["Standard Cartesian coordinates; y-intercept means value of y where tangent line crosses x=0."],"visualRequirement":"optional"}

{"schemaVersion":"turn-plan/v3","question":"Find the y-intercept of the tangent to the curve y = x^3 - 2x at the point where x = 2.","givens":[{"id":"g1","symbol":"x","value":2,"unit":"","sourceText":"x = 2","provenance":"given"}],"unknowns":[{"id":"u1","symbol":"b","unit":""}],"derived":[{"id":"d1","symbol":"y","value":4,"unit":"","sourceText":"y = 2^3 - 2*2 = 8 - 4 = 4","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["g1"]},{"id":"d2","symbol":"m","value":10,"unit":"","sourceText":"dy/dx = 3x^2 - 2; at x=2: 3*4 - 2 = 10","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["g1"]},{"id":"d3","symbol":"b","value":-16,"unit":"","sourceText":"y = 10x + b; 4 = 10*2 + b; b = 4 - 20 = -16","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["d1","d2"]}],"qualitativeClaims":[{"id":"c1","claim":"The tangent line at x=2 has slope 10 and passes through (2,4), crossing the y-axis at -16.","expected":"b = -16","relatedQuantityIds":["d1","d2","d3"]}],"lawIds":["power-rule-differentiation","point-slope-tangent-line","y-intercept-evaluation"],"assumptions":["Standard real-valued differentiation of polynomial curve"],"visualRequirement":"optional"}

{"schemaVersion":"turn-plan/v3","question":"If y = sin(x degrees), that is the sine of x measured in degrees, find dy/dx at x = 60.","givens":[{"id":"x0","symbol":"x","value":60,"unit":"deg","sourceText":"at x = 60","provenance":"given"}],"unknowns":[{"id":"dydx","symbol":"dy/dx","unit":"1/deg"}],"derived":[{"id":"dydx","symbol":"dy/dx","value":0.0152,"unit":"1/deg","sign":"+","sourceText":"dy/dx = (pi/180)cos(x*pi/180); at x=60: (pi/180)*cos(60 deg) = (pi/180)*0.5 = pi/360 ≈ 0.0152","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["x0"]}],"qualitativeClaims":[{"id":"c1","claim":"The derivative of sin(x degrees) with respect to x is (pi/180)cos(x degrees), because the chain rule introduces the degree-to-radian conversion factor.","expected":"dy/dx = (pi/180)cos(x*pi/180)","relatedQuantityIds":["dydx"]},{"id":"c2","claim":"At x = 60 degrees, cos(60 degrees) = 1/2, so dy/dx = pi/360 ≈ 0.0152 per degree.","expected":"pi/360 ≈ 0.0152","relatedQuantityIds":["dydx","x0"]}],"lawIds":["chain-rule","derivative-of-sine","degree-to-radian-conversion"],"assumptions":["x is measured in degrees, so the argument of sine must be converted to radians before applying the standard derivative rule","The standard result d/du sin(u) = cos(u) applies when u is in radians"],"visualRequirement":"none"}

{"schemaVersion":"turn-plan/v3","question":"If y = sin(x degrees), that is the sine of x measured in degrees, find dy/dx at x = 60.","givens":[{"id":"x0","symbol":"x","value":60,"unit":"deg","sourceText":"at x = 60","provenance":"given"}],"unknowns":[{"id":"dydx","symbol":"dy/dx","unit":"1/deg"}],"derived":[{"id":"d1","symbol":"dy/dx","value":0.0152249,"unit":"1/deg","sourceText":"(pi/180)*cos(60 deg) = (pi/180)*(1/2) = pi/360 ≈ 0.0152249","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["x0"]}],"qualitativeClaims":[{"id":"c1","claim":"Converting degrees to radians, y = sin(pi x/180), so dy/dx = (pi/180) cos(pi x/180).","expected":"dy/dx = (pi/180) cos(pi x/180)","relatedQuantityIds":["dydx"]},{"id":"c2","claim":"At x = 60 degrees, cos(60°) = 1/2, giving dy/dx = pi/360 ≈ 0.01522 per degree.","expected":"pi/360 ≈ 0.01522","relatedQuantityIds":["dydx","x0"]}],"lawIds":["chain rule","derivative of sine","degree-to-radian conversion"],"assumptions":["x is measured in degrees, so the argument of sine is pi*x/180 radians","cos(60°) = 1/2 exactly"],"visualRequirement":"none"}

{"schemaVersion":"turn-plan/v3","question":"Find the distance between the parallel lines 3x + 4y - 5 = 0 and 6x + 8y + 15 = 0.","givens":[{"id":"g1","symbol":"L1","value":"3x + 4y - 5 = 0","provenance":"given","sourceText":"3x + 4y - 5 = 0"},{"id":"g2","symbol":"L2","value":"6x + 8y + 15 = 0","provenance":"given","sourceText":"6x + 8y + 15 = 0"}],"unknowns":[{"id":"d","symbol":"d","unit":"units"}],"derived":[{"id":"d","symbol":"d","value":3.5,"unit":"units","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["g1","g2"],"sourceText":"L2/2: 3x+4y+7.5=0; d=|7.5-(-5)|/sqrt(3^2+4^2)=12.5/5=2.5"}],"qualitativeClaims":[{"id":"c1","claim":"Lines are parallel since coefficients are proportional (6/3=8/4=2).","expected":"parallel","relatedQuantityIds":["g1","g2"]},{"id":"c2","claim":"Distance between parallel lines Ax+By+C1=0 and Ax+By+C2=0 is |C2-C1|/sqrt(A^2+B^2).","expected":"d=|C2-C1|/sqrt(A^2+B^2)","relatedQuantityIds":["d"]}],"lawIds":["distance_between_parallel_lines","point_to_line_distance"],"assumptions":["Normalize L2 by dividing by 2 to match coefficients of L1"],"visualRequirement":"optional"}

{"schemaVersion":"turn-plan/v3","question":"Find the distance between the parallel lines 3x + 4y - 5 = 0 and 6x + 8y + 15 = 0.","givens":[{"id":"g1","symbol":"L1","value":"3x + 4y - 5 = 0","sourceText":"3x + 4y - 5 = 0","provenance":"given"},{"id":"g2","symbol":"L2","value":"6x + 8y + 15 = 0","sourceText":"6x + 8y + 15 = 0","provenance":"given"}],"unknowns":[{"id":"u1","symbol":"d","unit":"units"}],"derived":[{"id":"d1","symbol":"d","value":3.5,"unit":"units","sourceText":"d = |15 - (-10)| / sqrt(6^2 + 8^2) = 25 / 10 = 3.5","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["g1","g2"]}],"qualitativeClaims":[{"id":"c1","claim":"The lines are parallel because their coefficients are proportional: 6/3 = 8/4 = 2.","expected":"parallel","relatedQuantityIds":["g1","g2"]},{"id":"c2","claim":"Rewrite L1 as 6x + 8y - 10 = 0 to match coefficients with L2.","expected":"6x + 8y - 10 = 0","relatedQuantityIds":["g1"]},{"id":"c3","claim":"Distance between parallel lines Ax+By+C1=0 and Ax+By+C2=0 is |C2-C1|/sqrt(A^2+B^2).","expected":"d = |15 - (-10)| / sqrt(36+64) = 25/10 = 2.5","relatedQuantityIds":["u1","d1"]}],"lawIds":["distance_between_parallel_lines","pythagorean_norm"],"assumptions":["Lines are in standard Euclidean plane","Coefficients are exact integers"],"visualRequirement":"optional"}

{"schemaVersion":"turn-plan/v3","question":"Find the area enclosed between the curves y = x^2 and y = 2x.","givens":[{"id":"c1","symbol":"y1","value":"x^2","provenance":"given","sourceText":"y = x^2"},{"id":"c2","symbol":"y2","value":"2x","provenance":"given","sourceText":"y = 2x"}],"unknowns":[{"id":"A","symbol":"A","unit":"square units"}],"derived":[{"id":"x1","symbol":"x_1","value":0,"provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["c1","c2"],"sourceText":"x^2 = 2x => x(x-2)=0 => x=0"},{"id":"x2","symbol":"x_2","value":2,"provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["c1","c2"],"sourceText":"x^2 = 2x => x(x-2)=0 => x=2"},{"id":"A","symbol":"A","value":1.3333333333333333,"unit":"square units","sign":"positive","provenance":"derived","dependsOn":["x1","x2","c1","c2"],"sourceText":"A = ∫_0^2 (2x - x^2) dx = [x^2 - x^3/3]_0^2 = 4 - 8/3 = 4/3"}],"qualitativeClaims":[{"id":"cl1","claim":"The curves intersect where x^2 = 2x, giving x = 0 and x = 2; intersection points are (0,0) and (2,4).","expected":"(0,0) and (2,4)","relatedQuantityIds":["x1","x2"]},{"id":"cl2","claim":"On the interval (0,2), the line y = 2x lies above the parabola y = x^2, so the integrand is 2x - x^2.","expected":"2x >= x^2 on [0,2]","relatedQuantityIds":["c1","c2","x1","x2"]},{"id":"cl3","claim":"The enclosed area equals the definite integral of (top - bottom) from 0 to 2, which evaluates to 4/3 square units.","expected":"A = ∫_0^2 (2x - x^2) dx = 4/3","relatedQuantityIds":["A","x1","x2"]}],"lawIds":["intersection-of-curves","definite-integral-area-between-curves","fundamental-theorem-of-calculus"],"assumptions":["Work in the standard Cartesian plane with real x.","Area means the finite region bounded by both curves between their intersection points."],"visualRequirement":"required"}
